page.title: Sign-in and registration
page.lead: Who can get into the installation and how: registration, password, single sign-on and mail.

locked.note: Every value in this section is set by the server environment. To change it, edit the environment variables and restart the server.

failure.setting_locked: This value is set by the environment and cannot be changed here.
failure.last_login_method: You cannot remove the last sign-in method: nobody could sign in afterwards. Enable the password or another sign-in first.
failure.forbidden: You do not have permission for this action.
failure.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
failure.csrf_failed: Your session is stale. Refresh the page and try again.
failure.input_invalid: The server did not accept the values. Check the form fields.
failure.network: No connection to the server. Check your network and try again.
failure.unknown: Something went wrong. Try again later.

registration.title: Registration
registration.sub: Who can create an account on their own.

invite.title: By invitation
invite.body: Accounts are created only from an invitation link. The recommended mode.

domains.title: For email domains
domains.body: Only addresses from the domain list can register, for example hse.ru.

open.title: Open
open.body: Anyone with an email address can register.

closed.title: Closed
closed.body: Self-registration is off; an administrator creates accounts.

registration.domainsHint: Separated by commas or spaces, without @.
registration.domainsInvalid: This does not look like a domain: {{list}}.
registration.approvalHint: A new account waits in the approval queue until an administrator allows sign-in.
registration.noSmtpDomains: Mail is not configured, so an address cannot be confirmed by email. New accounts by domain will wait for administrator approval.
registration.openWarning: Anyone will be able to create an account and use build resources. Turn on approval if the installation is reachable from the internet.
registration.closedNote: New people can only appear through an administrator invitation or single sign-on.

signin.title: Sign-in methods
signin.sub: How people prove who they are when signing in.
signin.passwordHint: People sign in with email and password. If turned off, only single sign-on remains.
signin.onlyMethod: This is the only sign-in method. To turn off the password, enable a single sign-on provider first.
signin.disableWarning: After saving, password sign-in stops working for everyone, including you. Make sure single sign-on is set up and you can use it.

oidc.title: Single sign-on (OIDC)
oidc.sub: Sign-in through your organization's external service. The client secret is saved once and never shown.

empty.title: No providers yet
empty.body: Add a provider and a single sign-on button appears on the sign-in screen.

confirm.title: Delete the provider?
confirm.body: Provider “{{name}}” disappears from the sign-in screen. Accounts linked to it stay, but they cannot sign in through it. Type the name to confirm.

form.lead: Take the values from the application settings at your provider (Keycloak, Authentik, Google and similar).
form.label: Button name
form.labelHint: This is how the button is labelled on the sign-in screen.
form.issuerHint: The address without /.well-known: the settings are discovered automatically.
form.secretHint: Write-only: it is accepted and never shown again.
form.scopesHint: Separated by spaces. openid is required, usually email and profile too.
form.enabledHint: A disabled provider is kept, but nobody can sign in through it.
form.provisionHint: A person without an account gets one on first sign-in. Without it only existing accounts can sign in.
form.redirectNew: Register it with the provider. {id} is replaced by the provider ID, which appears after saving.
form.redirectHint: Register this address with the provider as an allowed redirect URI.
form.noBaseUrl: The public address of the installation is not set, so the redirect URI cannot be built. Set the public address in the server settings.

issue.issuerInvalid: This does not look like an address. Use the form https://id.example.org without parameters.
issue.issuerInsecure: https is required. Plain http is allowed only for localhost.

smtp.title: Mail (SMTP)
smtp.sub: Confirmation, password reset and invitation emails go through it.
smtp.offNote: Until mail is configured, confirmation and reset links are shown on screen, and the by-domain registration mode requires approval.
smtp.passwordHint: Write-only: it is never shown again.

issue.fromInvalid: This does not look like an email address.

test.title: Test email
test.sub: Checks the saved settings. Leave the address empty to send it to yourself.
test.needSmtp: Set the server and save the settings first.
test.saveFirst: Save your changes first: the test checks the saved settings.

smtp.usernameHint: The account that sends the emails.
smtp.fromAddressHint: People see this address in the From field.
smtp.fromNameHint: Shown next to the address, for example Department Studio.

loadFailedBody: Check the connection to the server and try again.
